rows.section: Case study card: Waterloo Remote Monitoring (SR&ED claims)
rows.before:
Waterloo Remote Monitoring — A Grant Nobody Mentioned

The problem: A remote patient monitoring company had filed two SR&ED claims prepared by a contingency-fee firm. Neither claim mentioned the provincial health innovation funding and hospital partnership payments the company had received across the same periods. The claims had been paid, the cash had been spent on payroll, and a review had just opened on the second year.

What we did: We read the funding agreements, applied ITA subsection 127(11.1) to work out which payments were assistance and by how much they reduced the qualified expenditures, and put a corrected position forward ourselves rather than waiting to be told. We then rebuilt the project records so the third claim separated the systematic investigation from the clinical validation work.

The result:

  • Assistance reduction quantified and disclosed proactively
  • Third claim filed with validation work properly excluded
  • Contemporaneous project records in place from that quarter
rows.note: Sales-proof case study of the firm handling SR&ED claims; nothing informational left about the firm. Sharad to confirm.
